bottom: Hobbs runs the best funded campaign in the race and leans on national party money routed through a county party, but the single interest with both large money and a live decision on her desk is a state contractor, not a national donor.

**Sunshine Residential Homes, the state's largest group home provider.** About $550,000 in gifts across her inaugural fund or 2022 campaign, a legal defense fund and the state Democratic Party, set against Department of Child Safety rate increases from $149 to $234 per bed. The attorney general found no quid pro quo on August 21, 2026. The Auditor General probe is still open, and the next governor sets DCS rates and renewals.

**The Democratic Governors Association and the Navajo County Democratic Committee.** A $10 million pledge on July 28, 2026, grown to $14 million by October 19, inside more than $33 million in county party spending for Hobbs and other Democrats. The lever is less a policy than a governor who blocks a Republican trifecta, measured by her record 541 vetoes.

**Utilities.** Arizona Public Service gave $250,000 to her 2023 inaugural, the largest named gift there, alongside Salt River Project and Tucson Electric Power. Her ads now claim she reduced electricity bills.

Biggs is a low budget candidate carried by one outside group. His own committee raised about $2.8 million through June, while Turning Point Action spent $18.3 million in a single month attacking Hobbs and promoting him.

**Turning Point Action.** From about $459,000 in 2025 to $18.3 million in the month before October 20, 2026. Its live interests are election administration bills, the border task force he promises and the veto pen he would remove. Its 2025 ad money ran largely through 1Ten LLC, owned by state Sen. Jake Hoffman, who later subpoenaed Hobbs over the Sunshine Residential affair.

**Club for Growth and the Arizona Freedom Club PAC.** Endorsements rather than documented checks. The live decisions are his pledge to phase out the individual income tax and to protect Empowerment Scholarship Account vouchers.

**Trump world.** Trump, JD Vance, Doug Ducey and Jan Brewer endorsed him. In Congress he voted Aye on H.R. 1 on July 3, 2025, and as governor he would run the state Medicaid program that law reshapes.

D.t: Katie Hobbs leads by 9.3 in the forecast and wins 95% of simulations. The cushion is about 297,559 votes; a one point swing is about 15,929 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +2.1 and D +16.7. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +7.9. Your best recent poll is HighGround Inc. at D +15.1; your worst is GQR for Hobbs (D) at D +2.6. 11 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Maricopa, a projected net 254,862 votes; Pima, a projected net 138,343 votes; Coconino, a projected net 23,476 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Yuma, R +3.9, 2.0% of the vote; Cochise, R +9.7, 1.8% of the vote; Navajo, R +3.1, 1.5% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Katie Hobbs runs furthest behind in Yavapai, Pinal, Mohave. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: Large counties, 82% of voters, 56 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.10 points; White voters, 74% of voters, 49 to 49, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.71 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 66% of voters, 53 to 44, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.30 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Katie Hobbs: Immigration voters 23 to 74, Midsize counties 41 to 56, White voters 49 to 49. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.4M cash against $1.2M. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 37% of the 1,543,211 ballots in Arizona so far, against 38% for the other party. That is 2.6 points better for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.2 points toward Katie Hobbs. Bank it: chase the remaining mail ballots and low propensity voters who have not voted.

visits.note: Launched a canvass for the Copper State Victory coordinated campaign ahead of the start of voting.
Spoke with Attorney General Kris Mayes to Arizona AFL CIO and AFSCME members before they canvassed metro Phoenix.
Rally at Laughlin Bullhead International Airport for Biggs and local Republicans.
Spoke before President Trump at a rally at Laughlin Bullhead International Airport.
Met voters about Pima County Republican turnout and his platform on affordability and public safety.
Rallied volunteers at a Copper State Victory canvass launch for the early vote weekend of action, per her campaign.
Toured Tovar Farms and discussed water security and costs for farmers, per her campaign.
Joined running mate Sine Kerr and Turning Point Action volunteers at a Ballot Chase kickoff at the State Capitol.
Held a canvass launch at the Mesa Copper State Victory office and sent volunteers out to talk with voters, per her campaign.
Spoke at a get out the vote rally hosted by Sine Kerr with Alexander Kolodin, Warren Petersen and State Sen. Tim Dunn.
Rallied supporters at the Landmark Event Center with John Giles, Sen. Mark Kelly, JoAnna Mendoza, Jonathan Nez and Gila River Gov. Stephen Roe Lewis.
Campaigned at Yuma County Republican Party headquarters, pledging that Yuma's water would be protected.
